stem: A newborn boy has seizures on day 2, with a serum calcium of 6.2 mg/dL. A chest radiograph shows no thymic shadow, and echocardiography shows a truncus arteriosus. Immunologic work-up confirms a failure of T-cell development.
oneliner: Newborn M + seizures with low calcium + no thymic shadow + truncus arteriosus + no T cells → which structure forms the thymus?
ask: Which embryonic structure gives rise to the missing thymus?

whyNot.A: Forms the **middle ear cavity and Eustachian tube**
whyNot.C: Forms the **superior parathyroids**, not the thymus
whyNot.E: An **arch** (mesoderm and neural crest): stylopharyngeus and greater horn of the hyoid, not an endodermal pouch

answer: Third pharyngeal pouch (thymus and inferior parathyroids)
why: The **third pharyngeal pouch** forms the **thymus and the inferior parathyroid glands**; the fourth pouch makes the superior parathyroids. Defective development of the third and fourth pouches with the neural-crest-derived **outflow tract** gives **DiGeorge syndrome** (22q11 deletion): **no T cells, hypocalcemia, truncus arteriosus**.

idea.rule: Third pouch makes the thymus and inferior parathyroids; fourth pouch makes the superior parathyroids.
also: First pouch: middle ear and Eustachian tube
Fourth pouch: superior parathyroids and ultimobranchial body (C cells)
DiGeorge: 22q11.2 deletion, with conotruncal defects, hypocalcemia, absent thymus
